subject.title: [Feature]: Async voice notes in the mobile chat composer (record and send as audio attachment)

question: Should OpenClaw accept scoped async voice notes in the first-party iOS and Android chat composers now, using client-side recording plus existing chat.send audio attachments?
rationale: This is a new native mobile input mode with protected maintainer labeling, UX choices, microphone ownership coordination, and platform proof requirements that automation should not decide alone.

options.title: Accept scoped mobile v1 after proof
options.body: Proceed with the iOS and Android PRs once each has maintainer review and redacted proof of recording, staging, sending, and rendering through the existing attachment path.

options.title: Stage one platform first
options.body: Land only one platform initially to validate UX, mic coordination, and proof expectations before committing to the sibling implementation.

options.title: Defer first-party voice notes
options.body: Keep users on Talk mode or third-party channel voice notes until maintainers explicitly prioritize async mobile voice input.

recommendation.title: Accept scoped mobile v1 after proof
recommendation.body: Proceed with the iOS and Android PRs once each has maintainer review and redacted proof of recording, staging, sending, and rendering through the existing attachment path.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the issue, both open platform PRs, and the strongest recent adjacent mobile chat/voice history in the inspected evidence.
